1: Exactly one tangent plane. For P on a sphere centered at C, the unique plane through P normal to CP is tangent. Any tangent plane through this sphere point must have P as its sole contact and this normal.
2: Infinitely many tangent planes. With C=0 and |P|=d>R, a unit normal n gives a tangent plane n.X=R through P precisely when n.P=R. These normals form a nondegenerate circle, giving infinitely many distinct planes.
